subject: Follow-up: Structured output & tool-calling qualification — next steps
summary: Post-discovery recap and technical qualification for structured JSON output and function-calling. Agreement to run a 500-sample eval, measure schema pass rate, latency and token cost, and validate retry/fallback behavior for tool-calls. Workshop to be scheduled with SEs and procurement/Security ask for SOC2 evidence.
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up: Structured output & tool-calling qualification — next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — good session. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Goal: extract structured invoice/payment records and emit a validated JSON payload per document to drive Acme's downstream ETL.
- Targets: schema-valid output >= 95% on first pass, critical-field correctness (vendor, total, invoice_date) >= 98%, latency target p95 < 400ms, sustained throughput ~10 TPS.
- Constraints: must run inside our Dedicated or Private deployment for PII/retention; procurement will need SOC2 + audit logs.

Immediate proposal
1) Eval: Redwood runs a 500-sample eval (your sample data) across two model profiles + our structured output harness. We’ll report: schema pass rate, field-level F1, p95 latency, tokens/output, and cost estimate.
2) Models to try: rw-calliope-13b-q4h (recommended starting point) and rw-calliope-7b-int8 (lower-cost variant). We’ll also include one larger open baseline (open-llama-3-13b-quant) for quality comparisons.
3) Tooling: test both direct JSON schema prompting and function-calling mode (server-side schema validation + post-parse fixer). We’ll measure strict compliance and fallback needs.
4) Retries/fallbacks: default suggestion is 1 retry with exponential backoff for transient decode/kernel errors, plus automatic fallback to cheaper model for non-blocking failures.

Attachments: initial-prompt-set.json (prompt variations + expected schema examples). See related links for the benchmark harness we’ll run.

Next steps / Asks from Acme
- Please confirm the sample file we should use (upload attached sample or confirm current dataset).
- Confirm acceptance of the evaluation scope (500 samples, two profiles).
- Who should we include for procurement/security threads (SOC2 evidence)?

I’ll loop Marissa and Karthik for the eval orchestration — propose a 60-minute workshop next week to kick off if that works.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
[dylan_brooks@redwood.com]
[Attachment: initial-prompt-set.json (JSON, 28KB)]

Thanks Dylan — the recap looks right. A few clarifying items from our side before the eval:

Hi Priya — Marissa (SE) here, quick technical plan and answers to your retry/schema questions.

Evaluation plan (technical)
- Run the 500-sample job across three runner configs: 
  a) Prompt-only with in-prompt JSON schema + constrained sampling (rw-calliope-13b-q4h)
  b) Function-calling mode (preferred) where model returns structured output which we validate server-side and apply a small re-ask prompt if parse fails (rw-calliope-13b-q4h).
  c) Cost baseline: rw-calliope-7b-int8 with same harness for cost/quality tradeoff.

Measurements we will produce
- Schema pass rate (strict JSON Schema validation)
- Field-level accuracy (vendor, total, invoice_date) and F1 scores
- p50/p95 latency and tokens per output (to estimate cost)
- Retry/fallback counts and effectiveness (how often re-asks fix schema failures)

Retry & fallback behavior (proposal)
- If server-side JSON validation fails after initial parse
  - 1 automated re-ask using the function-calling reformat prompt (no extra human intervention).
  - If still invalid, automatic fallback attempt to the smaller model (rw-calliope-7b-int8) once.
  - After that, document is flagged for manual review.
- Billing: model inference charges will apply per attempt — we’ll report estimated per-doc cost across expected failure rates so procurement can budget.

Schema hardening suggestions
- Use a small prompt scaffold with examples and strict field-level instructions (examples in attached structured-eval-playbook.pdf).
- Server-side lightweight sanitizer: if only minor formatting issues (unescaped quotes, trailing commas), attempt a non-model parse-fix before retrying the model.

Deliverables following the eval
- A CSV with per-sample pass/fail and field errors (acme-benchmark-results-20261101.csv).
- A recommended production config (model + retry policy + batching parameters) and an estimated monthly cost at projected throughput.

Scheduling & next steps
- We can run the eval within 3 business days after SOC2 confirmation and a signed eval SOW (one-page).
- Propose a 60-min technical workshop on Nov 18 to walk through the harness and verification criteria; Karthik will run the session.

Attachments: structured-eval-playbook.pdf (contains prompt templates, schema enforcement flow, and example failure cases).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[marissa_cole@redwood.com]
[Attachment: structured-eval-playbook.pdf (PDF, 430KB)]
